chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Three (things) were given to the Prophets (peace be upon them): perfume, wives, and the siwak (tooth-stick).
ai.seo_question: What three things were given to the Prophets according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies perfume, marriage, and the siwak as distinct privileges granted to the Prophets, elevating these acts from mere habits to spiritual etiquettes. In Shia scholarship, this underscores the balance between asceticism and worldly enjoyment, affirming that Prophets engaged in natural human needs like hygiene and family life with divine excellence. It serves as a foundational text for the fiqh of personal grooming and the sunnah of using perfume, particularly for prayer and social gatherings.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Talha Bin Zayd, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Three (things) are which the Prophets<sup>as</sup> came to – the perfume, and the wives, and the brushing of teeth’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Talhah ibn Zayd who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Three things were given to the Prophets. They are perfumes, marriage and toothbrushes.’”
